sections.h2: Where does Ballard County sit, and where did it come from?
sections.html:
Ballard County fills the far western tip of Kentucky where the Ohio River meets the Mississippi, in the Jackson Purchase. The county's own site calls it the ninety-third county formed, established February 15, 1842, from parts of Hickman and McCracken, and says it covers 254 square miles. Wikipedia's Census-based total is 274 square miles, including 27 of water.

The first seat was Blandville. A courthouse fire on February 17, 1880 burned most early records, and Wickliffe took over as seat in 1882. A buyer or heir tracing an old parcel can ask the County Clerk which books survive from before 1880.

sections.h2: Which towns and neighborhoods share the same tax offices?
sections.html:
Barlow, Kevil, La Center and Wickliffe are the four cities, and La Center is the largest. Bandana and Lovelaceville are census-designated places. All of the 2020 population was classed as rural, and a single school system, Ballard County Schools, covers the county. Axe Lake Swamp State Nature Preserve, 458 acres in the Barlow Bottoms, is part of a 3,000-acre wetland complex.

Water marks three sides of the county. Across the Ohio River sit Pulaski and Alexander counties in Illinois, and across the Mississippi sits Mississippi County, Missouri. McCracken County, with the Paducah area, lies east of Ballard and Carlisle County lies south. Ballard is counted in the Paducah, Kentucky and Illinois metropolitan area.

Every one of these places pays through the same three courthouse-area offices:

  • Sheriff, 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe: bills and payments, (270) 335-3561 or (270) 335-5153.
  • Property Valuation Administrator, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: assessments and exemptions, (270) 335-3400.
  • County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, Wickliffe: appeals and, later, unpaid bills, (270) 335-5168.

sections.h2: Is the Ballard County population rising or falling?
sections.html:
It is falling slowly. The population peaked at 14,378 in 1880, fell 41.6 percent to 8,390 by 1890, stayed between 7,900 and 8,800 from 1950 through 2010. By 2020 the count had slipped 6.3 percent to 7,728, and the 2025 estimate is lower again at 7,594. In 2020 there were 3,228 households. Single-person households made up 29.3 percent, and 14.8 percent were someone 65 or older living alone.

A lien discovered late can stall a closing, so clear it before listing.

sections.h2: When does a Ballard County bill become late?
sections.html:
KRS 134.015 supplies one schedule for every Kentucky county, and Ballard County follows it unless the state allows a delay. Pay in full by November 1 and 2 percent comes off the bill. After that and through December 31 you pay the figure printed. In January 5 percent is added; after January, 10 percent.

The state revenue agency describes the aftermath. A bill unpaid at the end of the day on April 15 is passed to the County Clerk, which records a lien against the parcel. From then, interest accrues at 1 percent for each month, and clerk and county attorney fees are added. Under a delayed schedule each stage lasts a month, so confirm the dates with the sheriff's office.

sections.h2: How does a Ballard County owner's year run?
sections.html:
The Kentucky property tax year as it applies to a Ballard County parcel
Month or windowWhat occurs
January 1Value date for real estate
January 1 to March 1Real property listing window
First Monday in May, 13 daysPublic inspection of the tax roll
Day after inspection endsLast day to file an appeal with the clerk
25 to 35 days laterLocal board hears appeals for up to five days
December 31Bills due without penalty

No new listing is needed when last year's roll described a property fully and correctly and nothing major changed. A buyer's deed price can serve as the listed value for the next January 1.

sections.h2: How does a Ballard County appeal work?
sections.html:
An appeal opens with a PVA conference at 132 North 4th Street; the clerk cannot take a filing otherwise. Then you have until the workday after the roll's inspection period closes to file at the County Clerk. State your own opinion of value on the form, because the bill relies on it if it is printed before a decision.

  • Evidence to bring: descriptions of the land and structures, insurance policies, construction costs, nearby sales listings.
  • Anyone paid to speak for you needs recognized credentials and your written authority.
  • You may audio-record the hearing.
  • A higher value set by the board produces a supplemental bill for the difference.

An owner who never files with the local board, or files and then skips the hearing, cannot take the case to a later stage.

sections.h2: Do older residents in Ballard County get a discount?
sections.html:
Owners 65 and over, or classified as totally disabled, claim Kentucky's homestead exemption through the Ballard County PVA. For 2025 and 2026 it subtracts $49,100 from the assessed value; the amount changes every other year. Plenty of residents might qualify: the 2020 census counted 21.4 percent of residents at 65 or above, with a median age of 44.8, and the 2025 estimate of 7,594 people sits 1.8 percent below the April 2020 base.

An owner who never applied might be paying tax on value the state would exempt. A call to the PVA at (270) 335-3400 settles it.

Retail sales were $56.7 million in 2022, about $7,415 per resident, and accommodation and food sales were $3.3 million. Among adults, 93.9 percent finished high school and 18.4 percent hold a bachelor's degree or more. Computers are in 95.0 percent of households and broadband in 87.6 percent, which helps owners who want to research a parcel or an appeal online.

sections.h2: What does a Ballard County house cost, and who lives in them?
sections.html:
Census survey data for 2020 to 2024 show a middle owner-occupied home value of $145,800 and owners in 76.0 percent of occupied homes. Gross rent at the midpoint was $817 and household income at the midpoint was $66,164. The county had 3,209 households and 3,730 housing units in 2025. The 2020 count put the vacancy rate at 12.4 percent of units and a rental vacancy rate of 12.0 percent.

Employers are few: 155 establishments with 1,617 workers in 2023, up 19.2 percent in a year, paying $87.0 million. Commutes average 26.5 minutes, 15.9 percent of residents live in poverty, and 354 are veterans.

Of 195 employer firms in 2023, 5 were minority-owned, the county has 510 nonemployer businesses, and 91.9 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier. Households average 2.35 people, 12.3 percent of residents under 65 report a disability, and 6.0 percent of residents under 65 have no health insurance. No building-permit total was reported for 2025.

sections.h2: How do taxes work when a Ballard County house is sold?
sections.html:
Kentucky treats the tax as the owner's personal debt from the assessment date, and a delinquency lien, once recorded, can stay on the land for as long as eleven years whoever owns it. A closing agent therefore tends to pay the year's bill from the seller's proceeds. Ask how that year is divided with the buyer.

  • Sheriff: what is owed this year and in past years.
  • Clerk: whether a lien is on record.
  • Deed: add the next bill's mailing address, which KRS 382.135 requires.

Owners who inherited a river-county house or moved away and now owe back taxes can request a written cash offer. Any lien balance is paid out of the price.

faqs.q: Who do I pay in Ballard County?
faqs.a: Payments go to the Sheriff at 437 Ohio Street, Wickliffe. The county's page for elected offices lists (270) 335-3561 and (270) 335-5153.

faqs.q: How much do I save by paying early?
faqs.a: Two percent of the bill, provided the sheriff has the full amount by November 1 (KRS 134.015). After that date the printed amount stands through December 31.
The bill picks up 5 percent in January and 10 percent afterward. Once April 15 passes, the County Clerk holds it and interest of 1 percent a month runs.

faqs.q: Where is an assessment appeal filed?
faqs.a: File with the County Clerk, 132 North 4th Street, after your PVA conference. Filing closes the workday after inspection ends.

faqs.q: Is the homestead exemption a county program?
faqs.a: No, the state runs it. The Ballard County PVA, (270) 335-3400, takes applications from owners 65 or older or totally disabled, and the 2025 and 2026 amount is $49,100.
